title: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha: How India's Two Houses Differ

content: India's Parliament has two houses. The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is directly elected by voters, while members of the Rajya Sabha, the Council of States, are chosen mainly by elected members of state legislatures.
The Lok Sabha normally serves a five-year term unless dissolved earlier. The Rajya Sabha is a continuing body that is never dissolved, with a portion of its members retiring every two years.
Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, which gives it greater power over finance. For most other laws, both houses must pass the same bill.
